They describe different distribution windows and should not be treated as a universal release time. The distinction matters especially for readers using Japanese schedules to predict when a new episode will appear on their local streaming service. The long-awaited anime adaptation of PSYREN premieres October 5, 2026 . Crunchyroll lists the international simulcast for 7:30 a.m. PT, outside Japan and China. What time does PSYREN Episode 1 release? Crunchyroll has confirmed the international simulcast for October 5 at 7:30 a.m. PT , available worldwide outside Japan and China. In Japan, the TV broadcast starts at 11:00 p.m. JST and participating Japanese streaming services begin from 11:30 p.m. JST. Related reading: Chitose Is in the Ramune Bottle Cour 2 Release Date & Time . What the premiere schedule does not confirm Crunchyroll's October 5 simulcast listing establishes the opening episode's announced time. It does not independently confirm that every later episode will appear at exactly the same hour or that all regional catalogs display the same schedule. For future episodes, the local platform listing is the practical reference. What is PSYREN? Ageha Yoshina’s life changes after he finds a mysterious red phone card and his childhood friend Sakurako Amamiya disappears. His search pulls him into a deadly mystery connected to the secret organization known as Psyren. Where to watch The series will stream internationally on Crunchyroll in supported regions, worldwide outside Japan and China. In Japan, the official site lists services including Prime Video, Hulu, U-NEXT, ABEMA and others from October 5 at 11:30 p.m. JST, with some services potentially using different start times. Related reading: DARK MACHINE THE ANIMATION Release Date & Time . What to know before watching PSYREN is a new adaptation, so you do not need to watch an earlier anime first. It adapts Toshiaki Iwashiro's completed Weekly Shonen Jump manga, which ran for 16 collected volumes. The production has also announced that the anime is intended to adapt the original manga through its ending. Studio and main staff Satelight produces the animation. Katsumi Ono directs, Shin Yoshida handles series composition, Akira Okuma is responsible for character designs, and the music team includes Takashi Ohmama, Tatsuhiko Saiki and Shu Kanematsu. Why the red phone card matters to the mystery The announced story connects Ageha's discovery of a mysterious red phone card with Sakurako's disappearance and his entry into Psyren's dangerous world. That sequence makes the card an entry point to the central mystery, not an explanation of its rules. New viewers can begin with the anime without knowing the manga's answers; the published premise does not establish what every card means or how the larger mystery resolves. Related reading: The Vermilion Mask Release Date, Time & Where to Watch . PSYREN FAQ Is PSYREN a remake? No. This is the first TV anime adaptation of Toshiaki Iwashiro's manga. Do I need to read the manga first? No. The anime begins Ageha Yoshina's story from the start, so newcomers can begin with Episode 1. Will the anime adapt the full manga? Yes. The production has announced plans to adapt the original manga through its conclusion. Related reading: The World's Strongest Witch Release Date, Time & Where to Watch . Is an English dub confirmed? Crunchyroll lists the dub airtime as TBA . AniNextUp will update this guide when a release date is announced. entries.content: NOVEMBER 13 · ANIME MOVIE Expelled from Paradise Sequel Reveals Main Trailer and Beyond the Night Theme Song The new main trailer previews the sci-fi sequel and its theme song “Beyond the Night” ahead of the November 13, 2026 Japanese theatrical release. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official key visual by Masatsugu Saito. © Toei Animation · Nitroplus / Expelled from Paradise Society 2. Official announcement · Image source . Release at a glance Release November 13, 2026 Where to watch Japanese theaters Applies to Japanese theatrical opening, not worldwide streaming Still pending International cinema dates and streaming partners Release details checked October 13, 2026 · Official source JAPAN RELEASE November 13, 2026 FORMAT Theatrical anime film STUDIO Toei Animation New main trailer and key visual revealed The official film project has released a new main trailer and key visual for Rakuen Tsuihou: Kokoro no Resonance , the sequel to Expelled from Paradise . The footage follows Gabriel and fellow agents as they investigate the Fallen, while a preview of the new theme song accompanies the action. Character designer Masatsugu Saito drew the new key visual. The official site dates its main trailer announcement to October 12 and its theme song announcement to October 13, 2026, in Japan. Neither announcement specifies an exact publication time. The film remains scheduled for Japanese theaters on November 13, 2026 . “Beyond the Night” theme song: artists and release dates TeddyLoid wrote, composed and arranged “Beyond the Night.” It features Ayane Sakura , who voices Gabriel, and Nagi Inoue of Nogizaka46. The song arrives digitally on November 11, 2026 , with a CD release scheduled for November 18, 2026 . Related reading: Noa Is My Senior, and My Friend Anime: 2027 Release, Main Cast and First Visual . These updates concern the Japanese theatrical opening and music release. International cinema and streaming dates have not been confirmed in the announcements. What connects the sequel to Expelled from Paradise The conflict between DEVA's virtual society and people living on Earth's surface remains a useful lens for approaching Kokoro no Resonance. The sequel's pursuit of the Fallen suggests that crossing between those worlds continues to carry political and personal consequences. Returning creative staff offers continuity, but the announced premise should not be mistaken for a full account of the film's plot. Do viewers need to see the first film? Kokoro no Resonance is explicitly presented as a sequel to Expelled from Paradise . Its returning DEVA-versus-Earth setting and references to earlier events mean the 2014 film offers relevant background for Gabriel's investigation of the Fallen. The official synopsis does not establish that prior viewing is mandatory, but watching the first movie is the clearest way to understand the world and its history before the new theatrical release. Related reading: Fool Night Release Date: November 26 on Netflix . Planning to watch outside Japan November 13 is the confirmed Japanese theatrical opening, not a worldwide streaming premiere. No international subscription-platform date is established by that announcement. Fans outside Japan should look for a separate distributor or cinema notice before making release-day plans. When does Kokoro no Resonance release? Rakuen Tsuihou: Kokoro no Resonance opens in Japanese theaters on November 13, 2026. It is the long-awaited sequel to the 2014 science-fiction anime film Expelled from Paradise. What is the movie about? The sequel returns to the conflict between the virtual society of DEVA and life on Earth. Gabriel and other agents pursue the mysterious Fallen—former security personnel who escaped to the surface after the events involving Angela Balzac—expanding the world established by the first movie. Related reading: The Moon on a Rainy Night Anime: 2027 Release, Trailer & Cast . Who is making the sequel? Seiji Mizushima returns as director and Gen Urobuchi writes the screenplay. Masatsugu Saito handles character design, NARASAKI composes the music and Toei Animation produces the film, reuniting core creative staff from the original project. Where to watch The November 13 date currently refers specifically to the Japanese theatrical release . An international streaming date has not been announced, so AniNextUp is keeping theatrical and streaming availability separate until an official platform announcement is made. The continuation's emotional stakes come from how those relationships change, rather than from a new cast replacing the existing group. The announced weekly Netflix rollout also gives viewers time to follow those shifts episode by episode. Why Netflix gives two premiere dates October 1 in Pacific Time and October 2 in Japan can refer to the same worldwide launch viewed from different time zones. They should not be read as evidence of a delayed Japanese release. The weekly rollout also means that the premiere date is the start of the new story, not the day every episode becomes available. When does The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 premiere? Season 2 premieres worldwide on Netflix on October 1, 2026 PT / October 2 JST. Netflix's October anime announcement lists a weekly episode rollout rather than a full-season drop. Where to watch The Ramparts of Ice Season 2 is a Netflix release. Because the global launch crosses time zones, Netflix describes the premiere as October 1 Pacific Time and October 2 in Japan. Does the Netflix premiere date mean every episode is available? No. Netflix's announced schedule is a weekly rollout, so October 1 in Pacific Time and October 2 in Japan mark the beginning of the new season rather than a full-season release. Viewers looking for a later episode should check the local Netflix episode list instead of assuming the entire season arrived on the premiere date. What happens in Season 2? The story continues the intertwined relationships of Koyuki Hikawa, Miki Azumi, Minato Amamiya and Yota Hino. Koyuki has difficulty opening up to other people, while the more outgoing Minato disrupts the emotional walls she has built around herself. Netflix's Season 2 trailer focuses on the four friends as their feelings begin to shift and their relationships become harder to define, continuing the coming-of-age romance from the first season. Who created The Ramparts of Ice? The anime adapts Kocha Agasawa's manga. AniNextUp: Netflix release dates can display differently depending on local time zone. What Netflix’s season-two trailer adds The August announcement does more than repeat the premiere window. Netflix says the four central characters return to a story where several relationships begin to shift: Koyuki and Minato move toward feelings beyond friendship, while Yota finally tells Miki what he has carried for years. The trailer and key art present that movement as the continuation of an ensemble drama, rather than a change to a new cast or a separate adaptation. The announcement gives a direction for the season, not a complete account of how those conversations resolve. Netflix also lists the production team: MANQ directs, Hikaru Ishii is assistant director, Yasuhiro Nakanishi handles series composition and Miki Ogino designs the characters. Studio KAI produces the animation. These credits are useful when following a continuing series because viewers can distinguish confirmed staff from speculation about changes between seasons. Netflix labels the worldwide weekly start as October 1 Pacific Time and October 2 Japan Standard Time. These are two renderings of the same launch across a date boundary, not evidence that Japan has an extra episode or a one-day delay. Subsequent availability can still appear at different local clock times depending on the service and territory. Season 2 began in October, so this page now helps readers identify the continuation and its cadence. Netflix confirms weekly episodes; it has not stated a full episode count in the release notice. The local title page is the best source for a particular account’s current episode list, audio and subtitle choices. entries.content: STREAMING GUIDE Ranma 1/2 Season 3: Netflix Schedule, Cast and Watch Guide Season 3 of the MAPPA remake began in October 2026. Check how Japan’s late-night schedule relates to the US calendar, what Netflix has confirmed and where to start watching. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official Season 3 key visual. © Rumiko Takahashi / Shogakukan / Ranma 1/2 Production Committee. Official July 25 visual reveal . WHERE TO WATCH Netflix Release at a glance Japanese premiere October 3 late-night slot: October 4, 00:55 JST Weekly Japanese TV Nippon TV, Saturdays 24:55 JST Studio MAPPA Streaming Netflix after the Japanese broadcast; check local episodes Checked October 24, 2026 · Official Season 3 schedule announcement Has Ranma 1/2 Season 3 started? Yes. Season 3 began in Japan in the October 3, 2026 late-night television slot. Nippon TV lists Saturdays at 24:55 JST, which is Sunday at 00:55 on a standard calendar; the opening broadcast therefore fell on October 4 at 00:55 JST. The July production announcement confirmed that schedule together with exclusive Netflix distribution after the Japanese broadcast. A date listed as October 3 and a Japanese clock date of October 4 can both describe the same launch. What does that mean for viewers in the US? The first Japanese television start corresponds to October 3 at 15:55 UTC: 11:55 a.m. Eastern Daylight Time or 8:55 a.m. Pacific Daylight Time. Those are conversions of the television start, not independently announced Netflix upload times. The production says Netflix follows the broadcast, so it would be misleading to promise an episode at the converted start time. US daylight-saving changes later in the season also mean a fixed Japanese slot does not always convert to the same American clock hour. Where can you watch the season? Netflix’s own MAPPA anniversary announcement identifies Season 3 as coming worldwide and exclusively to Netflix. The anime’s Japanese production notice likewise says Netflix distribution follows the television broadcast. Use your local series page for the available episodes, subtitles and dubbed tracks. The official on-air site has separate season tabs, including older-season platform lists; services carrying an earlier season should not automatically be described as carrying Season 3 at launch. Related reading: My Happy Marriage Special Episodes: Release Date & Netflix Guide . Is this a weekly release or a full-season drop? The Japanese schedule is weekly, with the Netflix release linked to that broadcast. It is not an announcement that the full season appears at once. If you are planning a catch-up session, distinguish episodes already available in your catalog from later installments still awaiting their weekly release. Local broadcasters across the Nippon TV network also join on different schedules, so their listings may be behind the first Japanese broadcast without indicating a streaming delay. What is Ranma 1/2 about? Ranma Saotome and Akane Tendo are engaged through an arrangement made by their parents, but their martial-arts romantic comedy is anything but straightforward. During training in China, Ranma fell into the cursed springs of Jusenkyo. Cold water now transforms him into a girl, while hot water returns him to a boy. That complication feeds the misunderstandings, rivalries and slapstick around the couple. Season 3 continues this remake rather than introducing an unrelated protagonist or starting the story over. What does the Season 3 trailer reveal? Netflix’s June announcement highlights Ryoga Hibiki, whose rivalry with Ranma and feelings for Akane intensify in the new run. It also points to his newly mastered Breaking Point Blow. The July key visual surrounds Ranma, Akane and Ryoga with characters appearing in Season 3. Those are useful previews of the ensemble and the coming martial-arts complications, but neither a promotional image nor a trailer proves the season’s final manga chapter or the eventual resolution of the romance. Related reading: Suikoden: The Anime — Schedule, Cast, Trailer and Game Guide . Who are the returning Japanese cast members? Kappei Yamaguchi voices Ranma, with Megumi Hayashibara voicing his female form, while Noriko Hidaka plays Akane. Koichi Yamadera returns as Ryoga, and Rei Sakuma as Shampoo. The production’s season-specific cast list also names Toshihiko Seki as Mousse and Kaori Nazuka as Ukyo Kuonji. These are Japanese cast credits. For a dubbed version, consult the credits and audio options of the episode you can actually access rather than assuming that every language track follows the same availability pattern. Which studio and staff are making it? MAPPA produces the animation, with Konosuke Uda directing, Kimiko Ueno handling series composition, Hiromi Taniguchi designing the characters and Kaoru Wada composing the music. Rumiko Takahashi’s manga is the original work, published by Shogakukan. The official staff page separates credits by season, so a list copied from the first season can miss later production changes. The roles above are supported by the Season 3 production information, rather than inferred from MAPPA’s involvement alone. Related reading: So What's Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin? Release Guide . Where should a new viewer begin? Start with Seasons 1 and 2 of the current remake before Season 3. That is the clearest route through its recurring relationships, rivalries and running jokes. Watching an older Ranma adaptation can be enjoyable background, but it is not the same viewing order as continuing this MAPPA series. When searching Netflix, match the current adaptation’s season listing instead of using an episode number from a different version as your starting point. Watch the original official trailer The trailer below is the Season 3 video from Netflix Anime. Its original YouTube metadata records June 19, 2026, at 05:55:00 UTC−07:00, equivalent to 12:55:00 UTC and 21:55:00 JST. Its duration is 1 minute 40 seconds. This upload accompanied the earlier October release-window announcement, while the more specific October 3 late-night schedule came later. Keeping those announcements separate avoids using the trailer’s publication date as the season’s premiere date. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER ON YOUTUBE Netflix Anime · Official Season 3 trailer Open the original Netflix Anime trailer on YouTube → What is still unclear from these announcements? The cited releases do not establish an exact Netflix upload minute for every territory, a uniform set of language tracks, or a final adaptation endpoint. Do not read the weekly television slot as a promise of a full-season drop or an announced manga ending. The anime’s current on-air page is the reference for Japanese station changes; the local Netflix episode list is the practical reference for what you can watch now. entries.content: OCTOBER 4 · 2026 Reborn as a Space Mercenary Anime: Release Date & Where to Watch Reborn as a Space Mercenary is scheduled in AniNextUp’s Fall 2026 calendar for October 4. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official promotional visual. Artwork source: official release announcement . WHERE TO WATCH Crunchyroll Release at a glance Release October 4, 2026 Where to watch Crunchyroll; Japanese audio and English dub launch together Region and timing Licensed territories; local catalog times vary. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Crunchyroll’s English dub announcement Why this isekai has a different appeal The familiar transported-into-another-world premise is expressed through science-fiction game systems rather than a medieval fantasy kingdom. Hiro's mercenary work, starship combat and space colonies make the series a closer fit for viewers who enjoy space adventures alongside reincarnation stories. The same-day English dub is also a practical difference for viewers who prefer dubbed premieres. When does Reborn as a Space Mercenary premiere? Reborn as a Space Mercenary: I Woke Up Piloting the Strongest Starship! premieres October 4, 2026. Crunchyroll began streaming the first episode on Sunday alongside the Japanese release, and an English dub launches the same day. Where to watch Crunchyroll carries the series in supported international territories. The announced distribution covers most of the world outside Japan, China, Korea and Mongolia, although catalog availability can still vary by location. What is the anime about? After waking in the universe of his favorite science-fiction game, Satou Takahiro takes on the identity of mercenary Hiro. Instead of a conventional fantasy isekai adventure, his new life revolves around starships, space battles, colonies and dangerous jobs across an interstellar setting. Related reading: So What's Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin? Release Guide . What to check if you want to start with the dub Crunchyroll's same-day English-dub announcement establishes that an English version begins with the premiere; it does not guarantee every audio track in every country or establish the exact hour at which later dubbed episodes appear. Check the language selector and episode list in your own Crunchyroll catalog. The cast named below are the English-language performers, not the Japanese voice cast. Is there an English dub? Yes. Crunchyroll confirmed a same-day English dub beginning October 4. Kyle Phillips voices Hiro, with Kelsey Cruz as Elma, Emily Neves as Mimi and Jaclyn Thomas as Serena. What Hiro's mercenary work adds to the premise Hiro's new life revolves around starships, contracts and interstellar travel. His knowledge of the game-like setting offers a starting advantage, but the synopsis does not establish how his future missions unfold. This gives viewers a practical way to distinguish the series from fantasy adventures centered on magic and kingdoms. AniNextUp: Release timing and streaming availability can vary by region. What the October premiere confirms The October 4 date is the series’ Japanese television premiere, while the Crunchyroll listing is the practical check for international streaming in a viewer’s region. Those are related but separate schedules: a Japanese broadcast slot does not by itself establish when a licensed stream becomes available everywhere. Crunchyroll’s October 2 dub notice adds a second viewing track, but the announcement’s same-day premiere information should not be stretched into a promise that every later dubbed episode will follow the same regional hour. That distinction matters for a show whose long title can lead readers to assume “reborn” means a conventional fantasy-world reset. Hiro instead finds himself in a science-fiction setting with a capable starship and a mercenary’s choices to make. The available premise points to a working life built around contracts, equipment and travel through space. It does not make the show a simulation of real-world military procedure, and details beyond the official synopsis should be treated as interpretation. How to use the guide while the season airs For a first-time viewer, the most useful checks are the episode list and audio selector on the official streaming page. A platform may list Japanese audio, subtitles and a dub without offering every combination in every country. If an episode appears later than expected, compare the service’s local listing before assuming the Japanese TV broadcast was delayed. The series’ premiere has already taken place, so the date now serves as an anchor for catching up rather than a future appointment. The official materials establish the October launch, the streaming partner and an English dub announcement. They do not establish a final episode count, a complete season length or an identical dub schedule across territories. AniNextUp will keep those fields open until a production or distributor notice supplies them. That separation lets readers answer the immediate question—where to start watching—without confusing promotional announcements with a full season calendar. entries.title: The Record of a Fallen Vampire Anime: 2027, Cast and Trailer
entries.description: The Record of a Fallen Vampire premieres in 2027. See the official teaser, cast, staff, manga reading guide and what remains unconfirmed.
entries.content: NEW ANIME · OCTOBER 5, 2026 The Record of a Fallen Vampire Anime: 2027, Cast and Trailer The Record of a Fallen Vampire is officially getting a TV anime in 2027. The announcement includes a teaser PV and visual, the two lead cast members and the main production staff. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official teaser visual. © Kyo Shirodaira, Yuri Kimura / SQUARE ENIX / The Record of a Fallen Vampire Production Committee. Source: official anime project . Release at a glance Release window 2027; exact date TBA Format TV anime Studios ZERO-G and Liber Streaming / broadcaster Not announced in reviewed materials Checked October 24, 2026 · Original production announcement When will The Record of a Fallen Vampire premiere? The Record of a Fallen Vampire is scheduled to become a television anime in 2027. The October 5 announcement confirms the year, but not a season, month, date or weekly broadcast slot. A teaser and named production team give the project more substance than an adaptation announcement alone, yet neither establishes when episodes will arrive. As of October 24, a specific premiere date would go beyond the official information reviewed for this guide. Where can you watch the anime? No international streaming partner or territory list is named in the official teaser description. That means there is no confirmed Netflix, Crunchyroll or HIDIVE release to put on a viewing calendar yet. Pony Canyon publishes the promotional video, while ZERO-G and Liber handle animation production; those roles do not themselves identify the service that will distribute episodes in your country. Look for an explicit licensing or streaming announcement before treating a platform listing as settled. What is the story about? The central figure is Rose Red Strauss, the vampire king associated with the destruction of the Kingdom of Night a thousand years earlier. He is trying to recover his beloved queen, Adelheid, who has been sealed away. The official introduction places him in conflict with dhampirs hunting his life and the Black Swan, a powerful enemy. It also promises the gradual revelation of what happened a millennium ago, so the mystery of the past matters alongside the present-day battles. Who is the Black Swan? VIZ’s first-volume description explains the threat in more detail: the Black Swan inhabits a young human girl every 50 years and gives her the power to destroy the vampire king and queen. Each incarnation grows stronger. That premise creates a repeating danger across Strauss’s long search, rather than a single opponent he can simply outlive. Readers who want to avoid later manga revelations should stay with the first-volume synopsis; descriptions of subsequent books expose major changes in alliances and motivation. Why do some listings call Strauss Akabara? The Japanese anime credits identify the lead as Rose Red Strauss, voiced by Yuma Uchida. VIZ’s English manga listing uses Akabara in its synopsis. These are naming differences around the same central vampire king, not evidence of two protagonists or separate adaptations. For searches, the Japanese title Vampire Juujikai and the English title The Record of a Fallen Vampire lead to the same manga property by Kyo Shirodaira and Yuri Kimura. Who are the confirmed voice actors? Yuma Uchida plays Strauss, while Aino Shimada voices Bridget Irving Frostheart. The official teaser lists these two lead performers. Their presence should not be presented as a complete cast list: the queen and other characters mentioned in the premise do not gain confirmed voice actors merely because they are part of the story. Additional casting, dubbed-language performances and international audio options remain separate announcements to watch for. Which studios and staff are making it? Mankyu is responsible for directing and series composition. Animation production is credited jointly to ZERO-G and Liber, with character design by jimao and music by Evan Call. These are the roles listed in the original official video. The credits establish who is attached, but do not explain how the two studios divide individual episodes or production tasks. Call’s music credit also does not announce an opening singer, ending theme or soundtrack release date. Watch the official teaser The teaser is published by Pony Canyon, with ABC Animation Channel shown as a collaborating channel on YouTube. Original upload metadata records October 5, 2026, at 02:00:01 UTC−07:00, equivalent to 09:00:01 UTC and 18:00:01 JST. The metadata duration is 48 seconds. This timestamp describes the promotional upload, not an episode premiere. The title and description confirm television broadcast in 2027; they do not narrow the release to a particular anime season. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER ON YOUTUBE Pony Canyon · Official teaser Open the original official teaser on YouTube → Should you read the manga first? The source manga credits Kyo Shirodaira for the story and Yuri Kimura for the art. The official anime video identifies the original Square Enix edition as nine volumes. English readers can start with VIZ’s Volume 1 listing, which supplies the premise, creator credits and a Teen age rating. That label belongs to the manga edition, not an announced television classification. Starting at Volume 1 preserves the story’s gradual introduction of Strauss and the mystery surrounding his past. Is the original manga complete? Yes. VIZ’s series catalog identifies Volume 9 as the final volume, matching the nine-volume count in the official anime announcement. That gives prospective readers a bounded reading commitment rather than an unfinished monthly story to catch up with. You can read the original manga in volume order while waiting for the anime, although later book descriptions disclose twists that the first-volume premise keeps hidden. Completion of the source manga does not tell us how quickly the television adaptation will cover that material. What does the anime announcement leave open? The production has not stated an episode count or identified an adaptation endpoint in the reviewed materials. Nine manga volumes do not automatically imply nine episodes, a complete adaptation or multiple seasons. No broadcast hour exists to convert into a local viewing time yet. For the next meaningful update, follow the official anime site and social account, then check any future distribution notice for territories and language details. Those facts will determine when and how viewers can actually watch. Sources checked October 24, 2026: Pony Canyon’s original official teaser and description ; official anime website ; VIZ Volume 1 listing ; VIZ series catalog . entries.content: RELEASE UPDATE · OCTOBER 5, 2026 Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story Premieres January 2027 on Crunchyroll Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story now has a January 2027 premiere window, a new key visual and full PV, six additional voice announcements, and confirmed Crunchyroll streaming worldwide outside Asia. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases RELEASE WINDOW JANUARY 2027 · CRUNCHYROLL Release at a glance Release January 2027; exact day unannounced Where to watch Crunchyroll worldwide excluding Asia Region and timing Japan: TOKYO MX, BS Nippon TV and Yomiuri TV; local episode hours unannounced. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story official site · Crunchyroll’s trailer and January 2027 release announcement What the January window establishes January 2027 is a confirmed broadcast month, not an episode-by-episode timetable. Crunchyroll's announced rights outside Asia also leave Asian distribution as a separate question. Viewers should therefore distinguish the Japanese broadcaster list from the international streaming territories instead of assuming that one announcement covers every market. When does Red Riding Hood: A Detective Story release? The TV anime will begin broadcasting in January 2027 on TOKYO MX, BS NTV and Yomiuri TV in Japan. An exact premiere day has not been announced yet. Where can you watch it? Crunchyroll has confirmed it will stream the anime worldwide excluding Asia when the series premieres in January 2027. Related reading: The Detective Is Already Dead Season 2 . New cast announced The newly announced cast includes Takuya Sato as Jill, Atsushi Tamaru as Antonio, Motoko Kumai as Rodrigo, Kotaro Nishiyama as Paolo, Sakiko Uran as Thumbelina and Ryoko Shiraishi as narrator. They join Yume Miyamoto as Red Riding Hood and Akira Sekine as Pinocchio. Studio and staff Itsuro Kawasaki directs and writes the anime at BENTEN Film . Manami Minakata and Yuko Yahiro handle character designs, while Jun Ichikawa composes the music. What is the anime about? The series turns familiar fairy-tale settings into mystery cases. Red Riding Hood travels through the storybook world and repeatedly finds herself caught up in incidents, using her curiosity and sharp reasoning to solve each mystery. Related reading: Granite Waves Anime: Story, Cast, Episodes & Where to Watch . What the October announcement means for viewers The production now has a January 2027 Japanese broadcast window, a fuller cast and confirmed Crunchyroll distribution outside Asia. The exact first-airing day and streaming arrangements within Asia remain separate unanswered questions; the new promotional video does not establish either. Why the fairy-tale detective premise stands out Red Riding Hood's role is different from that of a conventional fairy-tale protagonist: the announced premise puts her in the position of investigating incidents rather than simply escaping a familiar danger. For viewers, that changes the central question from “what happens in the original tale?” to “how will this mystery be solved?” This is AniNextUp's interpretation of the synopsis, not a claim about the structure of any unshown episode. How to read the streaming announcement by region The January 2027 broadcast window and Crunchyroll's announced distribution rights answer two separate questions. Japanese broadcaster names identify domestic television outlets; “worldwide excluding Asia” describes Crunchyroll's stated streaming territory. Neither statement establishes which platform will carry the show within Asia. If you live in an excluded territory, wait for a separate local distributor announcement rather than assuming that the Japanese broadcast or Crunchyroll listing applies to you. Related reading: Manchuria Opium Squad Anime: Release Date, Story and Latest News . What to check when the first episode gets a date A specific premiere day, a local streaming time and available subtitle or dub languages are distinct details. Once a dated schedule appears, readers should check the official anime site for Japanese broadcast information and their regional platform listing for actual access. The confirmed January window alone cannot be used to calculate a reliable episode countdown. Editorial distinction: The viewing guidance above is original AniNextUp analysis based on the announced premise and distribution scope. It does not introduce additional cast, plot details, release dates or streaming licenses. Watch the official PV ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER YouTube · click to play AniNextUp status: January 2027 and Crunchyroll are confirmed. Exact premiere day remains TBA. entries.content: FALL 2026 · RELEASE GUIDE So What's Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin? Release Guide The goblin fantasy began in Japan on October 5, 2026. Here is how the weekly TV schedule differs from Japan’s advance streaming, plus the story, cast, official PV and manga guide. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official anime visual. © Nazuna Miki, Tsukasa Araki / Shueisha / Tengobu Production Committee. Official anime site . RELEASE DATE October 5, 2026 STREAMING Crunchyroll STUDIO BAKKKA Release at a glance Japanese premiere October 5, 2026 · TOKYO MX, Mondays 22:00 JST Studio BAKKKA Japan’s advance streaming ABEMA / Prime Video; one week ahead from Episode 2 International streaming Crunchyroll; check local availability Checked October 24, 2026 · Official schedule Has Reincarnated Goblin already premiered? Yes. So What’s Wrong with Getting Reborn as a Goblin? began its Japanese television run on October 5, 2026. The first TOKYO MX slot is Monday at 22:00 JST, equivalent to 13:00 UTC. The title also appears in Crunchyroll’s Fall 2026 lineup. This guide separates Japan’s broadcast schedule from platform availability, because an episode being scheduled on Japanese TV does not establish its availability in every country or on every subscription service. Japan’s weekly television schedule TOKYO MX lists Mondays at 22:00 JST. BS11 lists Monday at 24:00, and Sun TV Monday at 24:30; on a standard calendar those late-night slots fall on Tuesday at 00:00 and 00:30 JST. AT-X began on October 7 with a Wednesday 20:00 JST slot. These are different broadcasts of the same series, not four release dates for distinct editions. Use the broadcaster you actually receive when setting a reminder. Why are some Japanese services an episode ahead? The official on-air page gives ABEMA and Prime Video a one-week lead over terrestrial television from Episode 2. The opening release on October 5 at 22:00 JST included Episode 1 alongside Episode 2: the first episode was simultaneous with TV, while the second began the advance schedule. Other Japanese services started distributing after the television broadcast. This explains why Japanese platform listings can show different episode numbers on the same day without either schedule necessarily being wrong. Related reading: New Anime on Netflix in October 2026: What to Watch . Where should international viewers check? Crunchyroll’s announced lineup includes the series, but its local title page is the practical place to check current episodes, subtitles and audio tracks. Japan’s official streaming list also names services such as Hulu, U-NEXT and d Anime Store. Those domestic listings should not be turned into worldwide licensing claims. In particular, the Japanese Prime Video advance arrangement is not evidence that every international Prime Video catalog receives episodes a week early. What is the story about? Akira Yagami is an office worker trusted by his colleagues who dies while saving a child from traffic. He wakes in another world as a goblin, a species whose normal lifespan is only seven days. His unusual ability, called Octogenarian in the anime site’s English introduction, gives him a much longer life. As goblins around him die, he inherits their skills. Demons, elves and dragons eventually become part of the wider circle gathering around him. Related reading: Reborn as a Space Mercenary Anime: Release Date & Where to Watch . What makes Akira’s skill different? The contrast between a seven-day goblin lifespan and Akira’s eighty years is the premise’s central advantage. It gives him time to accumulate abilities that short-lived goblins cannot develop in the same way. That makes the setting more specific than a generic reincarnated office worker gaining strength: his growth is tied to the passing of others in his community. This is a reading of the published setup, rather than a claim about how any particular later battle ends. Who are the cast and staff? Kikunosuke Toya voices Akira, Yoko Hikasa plays Karen, and Azusa Tachibana plays Chloe. The Japanese cast also includes Banjo Ginga as Simon, Sayumi Suzushiro as Eirene, M・A・O as Dike and Wakana Kuramochi as Eunomia. Ryuta Kawahara directs the anime at BAKKKA, with series composition and scripts by Yuichiro Momose, character design by Hiroyuki Saida and music by Takenoko Shonen. These credits describe the Japanese production; dubbed-language casting is a separate matter. Related reading: My Happy Marriage Special Episodes: Release Date & Netflix Guide . What are the opening and ending songs? Sou performs the opening theme, Hello, while the ending is Chiisana Bokura by AHUB, known in Japanese as Eihabu. The production’s September announcement names both songs, and the main PV previews the opening. Their presence in promotional material helps identify the correct anime trailer when searching the long English title. A theme-song announcement should not be mistaken for an episode soundtrack release or a guarantee that a streaming service carries separate music videos. Watch the official main PV The main promotional video linked from the producer’s September 9 press release is on the Showgate channel. Its original YouTube metadata records September 9, 2026, at 03:00:17 UTC−07:00, equivalent to 10:00:17 UTC and 19:00:17 JST. The metadata duration is 1 minute 38 seconds. This is the upload timestamp of the trailer, not the October premiere. Use the original video below to distinguish it from reposts and older teaser uploads. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER ON YOUTUBE Showgate · Official main PV Open the original main PV on YouTube → Where can you read the manga? The manga is written by Nazuna Miki and illustrated by Tsukasa Araki. Shueisha publishes it in Japan through Tonari no Young Jump, while Yen Press publishes the English edition. Yen Press’s Volume 1 listing is a useful starting point if you want the source story without jumping into later plot developments. It credits Caleb Cook as translator and labels the book Teen. That is the manga edition’s rating, not an independently announced age classification for the anime. What remains unconfirmed in this guide? The reviewed release notices do not identify how many manga chapters the anime will adapt or where its season will end. Do not choose a manga starting chapter based on an assumed final episode: begin with Volume 1 for the original version, or wait for the adaptation’s coverage to be clear. For weekly viewing, follow the appropriate local service’s episode list. For Japanese broadcast changes, the anime’s on-air page and the receiving broadcaster are the relevant references. entries.content: FALL 2026 RELEASE GUIDE A Returner's Magic Should Be Special Season 2 Season 2 premiered in Japan on October 7, 2026, and streams on Crunchyroll with a same-day English dub. Here are the verified broadcast times, regional streaming details, story setup and official trailer notes. Release at a glance Japan premiere October 7, 2026 · Fuji TV +Ultra at 24:45 JST International streaming Crunchyroll simulcast; territory exclusions apply English dub Same-day launch on October 7 Details checked October 25, 2026 · Aniplex's Japan schedule · Crunchyroll's Fall lineup As of October 25, 2026, A Returner's Magic Should Be Special Season 2 is airing: its first episode premiered on October 7. If you are catching up, the useful distinction is between the Japanese television slot, which is listed using late-night 24-hour notation, and Crunchyroll's international simulcast time. The dates can appear to differ by a day even when they describe the same weekly episode. When did Season 2 premiere in Japan? When did Season 2 premiere in Japan? Aniplex's official broadcast and streaming notice lists Fuji TV's +Ultra block from Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 24:45 JST. In ordinary clock notation, 24:45 on Wednesday is 12:45 a.m. on Thursday, October 8. Japanese television schedules commonly keep a late-night program attached to the preceding evening's lineup; calendar apps that do not use hours beyond 23:59 may therefore display October 8. The official listing also gives Kansai TV's Thursday 26:15 slot, with the first episode at 26:25, Tokai TV's Saturday 26:00 slot, and AT-X's Saturday 9:30 p.m. slot. These are separate Japanese broadcasts, not separate premiere dates. Where can you stream the new episodes? Crunchyroll carries Season 2 as part of its Fall 2026 simulcast lineup. Its schedule lists the subtitled release on Wednesdays at 10:15 a.m. Pacific Time. That is a platform release time for the listed territories, not the Fuji TV broadcast time; the two schedules use different time zones and distribution windows. Crunchyroll describes its availability as worldwide except Japan, China, Korea and Mongolia. Catalog rights can vary, so viewers should confirm the show page in their own country before subscribing or planning a watch party. Where can you stream the new episodes? Japan also has a separate set of streaming options. Aniplex lists d Anime Store , d Anime Store Nico Nico Branch, d Anime Store for Prime Video, d Anime Store for LINE Manga, U-NEXT and Anime Hodai from October 7 at 25:15 JST. That converts to 1:15 a.m. on Thursday, October 8. A broader group of Japanese services, including FOD, ABEMA, Hulu, Lemino and Prime Video, is listed from October 11 at noon JST. Those domestic listings should not be mistaken for worldwide platform availability. Does the English dub release at the same time? Crunchyroll announced the English dub for the same day as the Japanese-language premiere: Wednesday, October 7. Its Fall lineup lists the dub airtime alongside the subtitled Wednesday 10:15 a.m. PT slot. The same-day announcement means viewers did not have to wait for a later dub launch, though an episode may appear at a different local clock time after conversion. Crunchyroll announced Austin Tindle as Desir, Sarah Roach as Romantica, Macy Anne Johnson as Pram, and Anastasia Muñoz as Azest in its cast-and-crew notice. Check the platform listing for the audio options available in your region. What is the Season 2 story about? The official synopsis continues Desir Herrman's second chance after humanity's defeat by the Shadow Worlds. Sent thirteen years into the past, he is reliving academy life and gathering three allies: wind mage Romantica Eru, swordsman Pram Schnaizer and ice magic knight Azest Kingscrown. Their task is to confront a Shadow World that has appeared again and correct the history behind it. The season's new setup adds Desir's nightmare of Romantica's death and identifies the Devil of Destruction as the figure connected to that fear. This gives returning viewers a clear new conflict without revealing how the group resolves it. Does the English dub release at the same time? Who is making the second season? Aniplex lists Taishi Kawaguchi as director, Takamitsu Kono for series composition and scripts, Hiromi Kato for character design, and Kenta Higashiohji for music. Arvo Animation is the animation studio, produced by HAYATE. The principal Japanese cast returns: Takuma Terashima voices Desir, Sayumi Suzushiro voices Romantica, Natsumi Fujiwara voices Pram, and Asami Seto voices Azest. These credits make it easier to distinguish confirmed production details from fan speculation about staff changes. What is the Season 2 story about? The opening theme is “Sorrow,” performed by FLOW. The official September 15 PV announcement says the video introduced the song's audio and revealed the new main visual, which places the returning party alongside new opponents. Crunchyroll's Official Trailer 2 was published on September 9, 2026. The official YouTube listing provides that date, but the accessible official source does not show the original upload time or timezone. AniNextUp therefore does not claim an exact trailer timestamp or add a VideoObject uploadDate. The trailer remains available above, and the date-only limitation is stated rather than filled with a guess. For new viewers, the simplest entry point is Season 1, which establishes the Shadow Worlds, the Shadow Labyrinth and the original timeline before Desir returns to the academy. Season 2 is a direct continuation, not a reboot or a stand-alone story. Viewers who only need the essentials can remember that Desir has already seen the world's collapse, has reunited with Romantica, Pram and Azest, and is trying to change the outcome. The official synopsis does not require readers to know the source web novel to follow the anime's stated setup. Who is making the second season? The confirmed guide details are the October 7 Japanese premiere, Fuji TV's Wednesday 24:45 broadcast slot, Crunchyroll's Wednesday simulcast and same-day English dub, the named core staff and cast, and FLOW's opening song. Aniplex and Fuji TV publish the Japanese schedule; Crunchyroll provides the simulcast, territory and dub information. The exact international episode timing can change by territory, while a second-cour order, total episode count, and a date for the season finale are not stated in the official notices reviewed for this update. Official trailer Crunchyroll's verified YouTube channel lists Trailer 2 as published September 9, 2026. Its official listing does not expose the original upload time or timezone, so AniNextUp does not assert a precise timestamp or mark up an unsupported VideoObject.

entries.content: FALL 2026 · RELEASE GUIDE Romelia War Chronicle: Release Date & Where to Watch Romelia War Chronicle premieres October 3, 2026 on Crunchyroll. Release date, studio and streaming details for Fall 2026. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases RELEASE DATE October 3, 2026 STREAMING Crunchyroll STUDIO Atra When does Romelia War Chronicle premiere? Romelia War Chronicle begins streaming October 3, 2026, ahead of its Japanese television premiere on October 5. The production is planned as a two-cour television anime, giving the postwar story more room than a single short seasonal run. Where to watch Crunchyroll carries the anime internationally outside Japan, mainland China and South Korea. In Japan, Anime Times, U-NEXT and Netflix begin streaming on October 3 at 9:00 p.m. JST. Regional release timing may vary. What is Romelia War Chronicle about? Romelia helped Prince Henri defeat Demon King Zelgis, only for Henri to end their engagement after the victory. Instead of treating the Demon King's defeat as the end of the story, Romelia returns to a homeland still devastated by war and decides to rebuild it herself. Her work includes organizing an army, restoring the economy and confronting political conspiracies. The premise therefore focuses on what happens after the traditional fantasy victory, when a country still has to recover from the damage left behind. Related reading: BLEACH: Thousand-Year Blood War Releases “THE LAST PV” . Why the October 3 and October 5 dates are different These dates refer to two ways of accessing the same series, not two separate premieres. The October 3 date describes the announced streaming rollout, while October 5 is the Japanese television broadcast start. For viewers outside Japan, neither date alone guarantees that an episode will appear at the same hour on every regional service. Check the listing for your country before planning to watch on release day. Why rebuilding is a different kind of challenge Romelia's return home puts military organization, economic recovery and political resistance on the same level as battlefield success. The premise asks whether a victory over a single enemy can become lasting stability for ordinary people. That gives viewers a way to understand the story's focus without presuming which rebuilding efforts will succeed. Who may enjoy Romelia's postwar fantasy? The official premise begins where many fantasy adventures end: after the Demon King has been defeated. Romelia's next tasks involve soldiers, reconstruction and competing political interests rather than a new quest to defeat that same enemy. Readers who prefer strategy and the consequences of war may find that emphasis more relevant than the broken engagement alone. This is AniNextUp's interpretation of the announced setup, not a claim about later episodes or Romelia's ultimate success. Related reading: Tokyo Revengers: War of the Three Titans Release Schedule & Where to Watch . Who is making the anime? Animation studio Atra produces the series. Koji Saito serves as series director, Aya Satsuki handles series composition and scripts, and KOHTA YAMAMOTO composes the music. Yuna Nemoto voices Romelia von Graham. Watch the official trailer The official promotional campaign describes the series as a postwar saga about a discarded noblewoman building a new future. AniNextUp will track the two-cour schedule as additional episode and streaming information is announced. See the Fall 2026 anime calendar for more confirmed releases. entries.content: NETFLIX ANIME · JANUARY 2027 Sakamoto Days Season 2 Release Date, Netflix, Trailer & Cast SAKAMOTO DAYS is coming back in January 2027. Netflix has confirmed the streaming service and released a new character trailer, but the exact premiere day has not been announced. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Image: official Season 2 character trailer thumbnail from Netflix . Release at a glance Premiere window January 2027 Exact date Not announced Where to watch Netflix Season 2 trailer Official character trailer Episode count Not announced Release details checked October 16, 2026 · Netflix announcement · Netflix Tudum update PREMIERE January 2027 STREAMING Netflix NEW UPDATE Official character trailer When does Sakamoto Days Season 2 come out? SAKAMOTO DAYS Season 2 premieres in January 2027. Netflix has announced the month, but it has not confirmed a specific day or release hour. Until the service or the anime’s production committee posts a dated schedule, January is the most precise confirmed window. The second season will stream on Netflix. The announcement does not give a separate release schedule for other services, so this guide will be updated if additional platforms or territory-specific dates are confirmed. What does the new trailer reveal? The official character trailer introduces three faces expected to matter in the next chapter: Etsuko Satoda, Sakamoto’s former teacher at JCC; Amane Yotsumura, a student at the assassin training institution; and Satoru Yatsumura, whose history is tied to Sakamoto. Netflix’s October update also revisits the season’s central setup: Sakamoto and Shin go undercover at JCC while members of ORDER face a dangerous assignment in Kyoto. Related reading: Bass X Machina: Official Full Trailer, Netflix Release Date & Cast . The trailer gives viewers a first look at those characters and the series’ mix of undercover comedy and assassin action. It does not establish an episode count, a weekly-versus-binge release pattern, or a full international schedule. Watch the official Season 2 character trailer ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Netflix Anime · YouTube The video is hosted by Netflix’s verified YouTube channel. Playback loads only after you press play. What is Season 2 about? The story follows Sakamoto and Shin as they enter JCC, Japan’s assassin training institution, to investigate the elusive figure known as X, or Slur. At the same time, ORDER members Nagumo, Shishiba, and Osaragi travel to Kyoto for an assignment that turns into an ambush. Netflix’s synopsis says the season will also bring the shared past of Sakamoto, Nagumo, Rion, and Slur into focus. That setup gives the sequel two connected threads: Sakamoto’s undercover work at the school and a wider conflict involving the assassin organization. The official materials point to those story elements without confirming how many manga chapters the season will adapt. Who is in the Sakamoto Days Season 2 cast? Netflix’s current Season 2 updates identify the returning characters Natsuki Seba and Akira Akao, alongside new characters Etsuko Satoda, Amane Yotsumura, and Satoru Yatsumura. The latest Netflix announcement does not provide voice-actor credits for every new character, so we are keeping the character list separate from unconfirmed casting details. Netflix previously listed the Season 1 Japanese leads as Tomokazu Sugita (Taro Sakamoto), Nobunaga Shimazaki (Shin Asakura), Ayane Sakura (Lu Shaotang), Nao Tōyama (Aoi Sakamoto), and Hina Kino (Hana Sakamoto). Those are Season 1 credits; AniNextUp will update this section when Netflix confirms the Season 2 voice cast. Where can you watch Season 1? Netflix lists both parts of Season 1 on its service. Catching up before January is the clearest way to follow Sakamoto’s move from retired hitman to shop owner whose old world keeps pulling him back in. What has not been confirmed yet? Netflix has confirmed a January 2027 return and its streaming platform. The exact premiere day, release hour, number of episodes, weekly release pattern, and a complete Season 2 voice cast announcement remain unconfirmed in the official sources linked here. We will revise the guide when those details are published. entries.title: Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Anime Shares Creditless Opening and Ending Videos
entries.description: Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 has released creditless opening and ending videos, featuring MADKID's Unbroken and nonfic!'s Sukipi no Okage!.
entries.content: OFFICIAL NEWS · 2026-10-09 Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Anime Shares Creditless Opening and Ending Videos Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 has released creditless opening and ending videos, featuring MADKID's Unbroken and nonfic!'s Sukipi no Okage!. By AniNextUp Editorial Team Release at a glance Release Season 2 began October 7, 2026 in Japan Confirmed songs Opening: MADKID’s Unbroken; ending: nonfic!’s Sukipi no Okage! Region and timing The production music pages confirm the songs. Physical record release dates differ from the anime premiere. Release details checked October 12, 2026 · Sasaki and Peeps official broadcast schedule · Sasaki and Peeps official opening theme credits · Sasaki and Peeps official ending theme credits Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 shares its creditless themes Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 has released creditless versions of its opening and ending animation. Crunchyroll reported the clips on October 9, 2026, following the season's Japanese television debut. The opening features MADKID's “Unbroken,” while the ending uses “Sukipi no Okage!” by nonfic! Both credits can be checked against the anime's official music page . For viewers following the new season, the clips offer a convenient way to revisit its theme sequences separately from the episodes. A creditless release removes the production names normally overlaid on the animation. It does not mean the animation has no credited creators, and it should not be confused with a newly announced episode or an extended edition of the television series. Where to find the opening and ending videos The two sequences are presented in Crunchyroll's October 9 announcement . Use the opening and ending sections there to locate the corresponding players. This article links to that announcement rather than inserting a video address that has not been checked against the release. Expect a television theme sequence rather than a full episode. These clips are best approached after starting Season 2 if you prefer discovering characters and situations through the story itself. Opening and ending animation can reveal imagery that a viewer would rather encounter in context, even when the accompanying news announcement contains no plot summary. MADKID returns with “Unbroken” The official opening-theme page identifies “Unbroken” as the Season 2 opening and lists it on MADKID's thirteenth single, “Unbroken / Bonbaraman,” with an October 14, 2026 release date. That date has already passed as of this article's October 26 source check; it is a music-product date, not a second premiere for the anime. The same page includes a comment from MADKID member LIN. In paraphrase, he says the lyrics were written with Sasaki and Peeps' thoughts, choices and changing emotions in mind, and describes working with Q-MHz on the song. This provides an attributable explanation of the track's connection to the protagonists, rather than asking listeners to treat a fan interpretation as an official statement. MADKID also performed the first season's opening, “FLY,” according to the series' music index. The new title therefore marks a change of song while retaining the opening artist. When searching music services or video platforms, including both “Unbroken” and “MADKID” helps distinguish the Season 2 theme from the earlier opening. nonfic! performs “Sukipi no Okage!” The ending's Japanese title is すきぴのおかげ！ , and its artist is のんふぃく！ , rendered here as nonfic! The official ending-theme page is the clearest reference when English reports display an unfamiliar spelling or a broken character in the group's name. That page lists a December 8, 2026 music release and describes a planned six-track product with multiple editions. In the accompanying artist comment, the group presents the theme as a bright, positive pop song about affection. Those details concern the announced release; they do not establish that every track or edition is already available internationally. The three dates serve different purposes: October 7 is the Japanese television launch, October 14 is the opening single's listed release, and December 8 is the ending product's announced date. Hearing a song in an episode before its physical release is not a contradiction. The creditless clip, commercial recording and television broadcast are separate ways of encountering the music. When Season 2 began and where to check streaming The official broadcast schedule lists an October 7, 2026 launch with a one-hour premiere. AT-X and TOKYO MX began that Wednesday, while BS Nippon TV's opening broadcast followed on October 8. These are Japanese broadcast dates, so they should not be read as a single worldwide streaming time. For Japan, the schedule also lists Prime Video from October 7 and a later rollout to additional services from October 12. Crunchyroll's announcement identifies the season as part of its fall simulcast lineup. Check the show's listing in your own region for available episodes, subtitles and audio options; a Japanese platform schedule alone cannot establish those details for another country. For the broader release overview, see our Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 guide . The anime release calendar provides a separate route to other seasonal releases. The series behind the music The official introduction follows an office worker whose pet bird is a sage from another world. Peeps gives Sasaki access to magic and travel between worlds, while supernatural encounters also complicate his life in modern Japan. The Season 2 staff credits name Yushi Ibe as director, Yamato Ouchi as assistant director, Deko Akao for series composition and Saori Nakashiki for character design, with animation by SILVER LINK. The adaptation credits Buncololi's original work and Kantoku's original character designs. These production details place the theme release within the continuing adaptation without implying another season has been announced. Sources checked October 26, 2026: official music, broadcast, introduction and staff pages, plus Crunchyroll's creditless-video announcement. Production references: official ending title and performer , Season 2 staff , Japanese broadcast schedule and official premise . entries.content: Home › Fall 2026 › Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 FALL 2026 · SEASON 2 Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Release Date: October 7 & Where to Watch Season 2 began in Japan on October 7, 2026. Here are the confirmed TV and streaming schedules, the difference between Japan and international availability, and the story and staff details. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Season 2 key visual. Source: official anime website . Release at a glance Japan premiere October 7, 2026 · first broadcast is a one-hour special Japan streaming Prime Video · Wednesdays at 10:30 p.m. JST International streaming Crunchyroll in its listed Fall 2026 territories; check local catalog Studio SILVER LINK. Schedule checked October 25, 2026 · official broadcast and streaming schedule When did Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 premiere? Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 began on October 7, 2026. As of October 25, the sequel is airing in Japan. The main practical detail is that there is no single schedule for every viewer: Japanese television, Japanese streaming services and Crunchyroll publish separate listings, and their clocks should not be mixed together. The official anime schedule lists AT-X on Wednesdays at 10:00 p.m. Japan Standard Time (JST), starting October 7 with a one-hour special. Tokyo MX also began that night at 11:00 p.m. JST, with a one-hour premiere slot. BS NTV's first broadcast was Thursday, October 8 at 11:00 p.m. JST. The difference is the channel timetable, not a second premiere for another season. For each station, the official schedule lists later installments in regular 30-minute weekly slots. Does the first broadcast contain two episodes? The official wording calls the opening a one-hour special. That describes the length of the Japanese premiere slot; it does not establish how every international streaming service divides or labels the material in its episode menu. KADOKAWA's schedule separately identifies the weekly 30-minute slots for episodes after the special. If a service displays one long premiere or separate episode entries, follow that service's listing rather than assuming the Japanese TV format guarantees two numbered streaming episodes. Related reading: Sasaki and Peeps Season 2 Anime Shares Creditless Opening and Ending Videos . Where can you stream it in Japan? The official anime website names Prime Video as the earliest, exclusive streaming service in Japan. Its schedule lists new episodes on Wednesdays from October 7 at 10:30 p.m. JST. The same official page lists a wider group of Japanese services beginning Monday, October 12 at 10:30 p.m. JST. The subscription services include d Anime Store, ABEMA, U-NEXT, Anime Hodai, Nico Nico, DMM TV, Lemino, FOD, Bandai Channel, Hulu, TELASA, J:COM STREAM and milplus. It also lists several pay-per-view stores. Availability can change, so use the linked service pages for current catalog status. These Japan-specific rights do not mean that Prime Video is the international platform in every country. Related reading: Anime Mysterious Codes (October 2026): New Halloween Codes & How to Redeem . Where can viewers outside Japan watch? Crunchyroll included Season 2 in its Fall 2026 lineup for North America, Central America, South America, Europe, Africa, Oceania, the Middle East, the CIS, India and Southeast Asia. The platform listing is the relevant source for those territories, while local catalog and language options should be checked in the viewer's country. The published lineup did not give one clock time that can safely be applied to every region. AniNextUp therefore does not convert a Japanese broadcast time into a claimed worldwide streaming time. That distinction matters if a calendar app shows October 7 in one place and October 8 in another. Japan's BS NTV broadcast begins on October 8, while AT-X and Tokyo MX start on October 7; international availability follows the local platform's schedule. A date-only season announcement cannot tell a viewer what hour an episode appears in a different time zone. What is Season 2 about? The official introduction starts with Sasaki, a tired office worker who buys a Java sparrow at a pet shop. The bird, Peeps, is a renowned sage reborn from another world. Peeps gives Sasaki magic and a way to cross between modern Japan and a fantasy setting. Sasaki uses that access to trade goods, run a restaurant and train in magic, hoping the other world can offer relief from corporate life. Related reading: Anime News: October 2026 — Releases, Sequels & Streaming Updates . The story then complicates that escape: on his way home from work, Sasaki encounters a person with supernatural abilities. He uses otherworldly magic to get through the encounter, is mistaken for an ability user himself, and is recruited by a Japanese government office dealing with paranormal phenomena. That premise explains the series' unusual mix of fantasy commerce, workplace comedy and modern supernatural conflict. Season 2 continues those threads with Peeps and the returning cast; the official synopsis, rather than fan speculation, is the safest guide to what the adaptation has confirmed. Who is making the new season? SILVER LINK. returns as the animation studio. The official KADOKAWA listing credits Yushi Abe as director, Yamato Ouchi as assistant director, Deko Akao for series composition and Saori Nakashiki for character design. Music is credited to Koji Fujimoto and Osamu Sasaki. The main Japanese cast includes Tomokazu Sugita as Sasaki, Aoi Yuki as Peeps, Akari Kito as the Neighbor, Rie Takahashi as Hoshizaki, Naomi Ohzora as Futari Shizuka, and Miyu Tomita as Elsa. KADOKAWA's full cast list includes the additional returning characters and performers. Related reading: BLEACH × Graniph: 17-Item Collection Launches in Japan on October 20 . What does the trailer confirm? The official trailer promotes the October start and the first-season setup; later promotional material gives the exact October 7 premiere and one-hour-special format. The trailer is useful for seeing the new visual and returning characters, but it does not replace the broadcast schedule. The official Crunchyroll YouTube listing shows a June 3, 2026 publication date. The accessible listing does not expose the original upload time with a timezone, so AniNextUp does not invent that precision or add a VideoObject uploadDate. The current official anime schedule is linked below for the details that affect when and where to watch. What is confirmed, and what remains unclear? Confirmed details include the October 7 start, a one-hour Japanese premiere slot, the station-by-station timetable, Prime Video's Japanese Wednesday release, the wider Japanese streaming rollout, Crunchyroll's listed territories, the studio, principal staff and cast. The official pages reviewed do not state a complete season episode count, a finale date, or a universal international release hour. Those points should remain open until the production committee or regional streaming service publishes them. Official sources Official anime website: Season 2 broadcast and Japanese streaming schedule KADOKAWA: Season 2 schedule, staff, cast and premise · KADOKAWA official series profile Crunchyroll Fall 2026 lineup and listed territories · Official Crunchyroll trailer The official trailer listing identifies June 3, 2026, but the accessible listing does not show its exact original upload time and timezone. No precise upload timestamp or VideoObject is asserted. entries.content: OCTOBER 19, 2026 · NEW ANIME Sekiro: No Defeat Release Date: January 2027, Episodes & Trailer Sekiro: No Defeat premieres as an eight-episode series in January 2027. The expanded television version follows the Japanese theatrical release and adds material that was not included in the film. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official TV anime key visual · ©KADOKAWA/Sekiro: No Defeat PARTNERS. Original game ©2019 FromSoftware, Inc. Source: September 25 production announcement . Release at a glance Series premiere January 2027 · exact day and time TBA Episodes 8 · expanded television version Streaming Crunchyroll · supported territories Animation studio Qzil.la Verified October 19, 2026 · Official TV anime website When does the Sekiro anime come out? Sekiro: No Defeat is scheduled for January 2027. The production's September 25 announcement confirms an eight-episode television series. The current official TV website repeats that window; the cited announcements do not provide a specific first-episode date or release hour. Where will Sekiro: No Defeat stream? Crunchyroll's announced release is January 2027, with weekly episodes. The announced territories cover the world excluding Japan, China, Korea, Russia and Belarus . Those exclusions matter when checking a local catalog. See Crunchyroll's series announcement and UnGeek's September 28 coverage of the streaming announcement . A detailed international timetable, dub schedule and language lineup are not established by the sources cited here. Related reading: Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Is Out on Netflix: Episodes & Trailer . How is the series different from the movie? The production explains that the project began as an eight-part series and was first presented as an edited theatrical version. The television version retains the film's story while adding new episodes, scenes and cuts. The Japanese film opened on September 4, 2026. That earlier cinema date refers to a different release format, while January 2027 is the window to follow for the series. Related reading: Granite Waves Anime: Story, Cast, Episodes & Where to Watch . Watch the official Sekiro: No Defeat trailer The official TV website links the theatrical trailer below. It was released on June 26, 2026: its September 4 date promotes the Japanese film, rather than announcing a precise day for the January series. ▶ WATCH OFFICIAL TRAILER Official theatrical trailer · TV series: January 2027 Watch the official trailer on YouTube → What is the story about? Based on FromSoftware's Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice , the anime follows the shinobi Wolf and his young lord, Kuro, in the land of Ashina. Kuro's Dragon's Heritage can grant immortality, drawing the attention of people seeking that power. Their struggle centers on loyalty, survival and the consequences of that bloodline. The official synopsis introduces the conflict; this guide avoids assuming which of the game's possible endings the adaptation will use. Cast, studio and production staff The TV anime's cast and staff page credits: Daisuke Namikawa as Wolf Miyuki Satou as Kuro Kenjiro Tsuda as Genichiro Ashina Shizuka Ito as Emma Takaya Hashi as Owl Kenichi Kutsuna directs, Takuya Sato handles series composition and Takahiro Kishida designs the characters. Animation is by Qzil.la, with production by ARCH. The music credits include Shuta Hasunuma and Ryuichi Sakamoto's “Blu” as the theme. What remains to be announced? The confirmed details are the January window, eight-episode format and announced streaming regions. A specific premiere day, episode-by-episode calendar and international release times should be checked against future production or distributor updates. The confirmed month should be distinguished from an exact-date announcement. The production has also shared an exhibition-match interview as Sunraku and his allies enter a new competitive arena. By AniNextUp Editorial Team · How we verify releases Official third-season key visual · ©Katarina, Ryosuke Fuji, Kodansha / Shangri-La Frontier Production Committee, MBS. Production announcement . Release at a glance Premiere January 10, 2027 · Japanese television Broadcast MBS/TBS network · Sundays at 17:00 JST Run Two consecutive cours · episode total TBA International streaming Crunchyroll announced · local timetable TBA Verified October 20, 2026 · Official premiere announcement When does Shangri-La Frontier Season 3 come out? The Japanese release date is January 10, 2027. The production announced the date on September 16, alongside the season's key visual. Episodes are scheduled for Sundays at 5 p.m. JST on the MBS/TBS network of 28 stations. This is the Japanese broadcast timetable. An international streaming upload may follow a different clock time, so viewers should check the distributor's local schedule before converting the television time into a streaming appointment. The platform announcement and the Japanese television premiere answer different questions: the first establishes an announced streaming home; the second gives the domestic broadcast date. The sources cited here do not establish a precise international release hour or dub timetable. How many episodes will Season 3 have? The production confirms two consecutive cours . That describes a run across two successive television programming blocks. It does not, by itself, confirm an exact episode count, a specific finale date or an all-at-once streaming release. What is the new season about? The official introduction takes Sunraku away from Shangri-La Frontier for a time. Oikatzo invites him to the Global Game Competition, where they join Pencilgon in the new VR fighting game Galaxia Heroes: Chaos . Their opponents include the powerful American team Star Rain. For returning viewers, the shift changes the immediate goal from overcoming a game's monsters to competing against skilled players. The production's new exhibition material highlights that contest without requiring viewers to treat promotional interviews as complete episodes. Official video: Nu2meg versus Lucas Garcia The production released this pre-match interview on October 15. The characters discuss their state of mind, their opponents and the coming match. Yuma Uchida returns as Sunraku, with Yoko Hikasa as Pencilgon and Makoto Koichi as Oikatzo. The cast also includes Minami Takahashi as Silvia Goldberg and Daiki Hamano as Lucas Garcia.
